newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT SAYS NO NEED FOR CROWN RATE CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT SAYS NO NEED FOR CROWN RATE CHANGES.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday said there was need to take any administrative measures to adjust the official exchange rate of the crown.

Government spokeswoman Ludmila Bulakova told journalists after a regular Tuesday government meeting that representatives of the central bank (NBS) briefed the cabinet on the latest market development with the crown.
"The outcome of this meeting with NBS officials was that both institutions saw no need to take any administrative measures that should change the rate of the crown," she said.
NBS officials present at the meeting were not immediately available for comment on the government statement.
The central bank has been fighting strong dawnward pressure on the crown which began about two weeks ago by foreign speculators looking to short-sell the currency.
Moves to support the crown included choking liquidity on the local money market and fixing the crown's official rate stronger than market levels during the attack on the currency.
The central bank's strategy appears to have stopped speculative short selling of crowns so far, protecting it against a strong decline.
The crown traded at around -0.50 percent in the depreciation side of its mark/dollar baske parity on Tuesday afternoon after the NBS fixed it at -0.67 percent against the midpoint earlier in the day.

But the NBS's moves have also effectively halted trading both on the money and the forex spot markets as banks were forced to limit their quotations to insignificant volumes due to an accute liquidity shortage.

Analysts have said a crown rate close to the official fixing levels appears artificially overvalued and predicted a decline of the currency after the NBS starts adding crown liquidity to the banking sector.
